date_note: Sisa Journal, published 25 November, says the FSC unveiled the draft the previous day.
title: South Korea's FSC unveils draft Digital Asset Basic Act with a maximum surcharge of 10% of revenue after hacks
summary: Korea's Financial Services Commission unveiled a draft Digital Asset Basic Act, Sisa Journal reports. If a business breaches its IT safety obligations and suffers a hack or similar incident, it could face a surcharge of a maximum of 10% of revenue. The draft also plans no-fault liability for user losses from hacks or system failures.
plain: Korea's financial regulator has drafted a law under which crypto businesses hit by hacks after breaching IT safety duties could face a surcharge of a maximum of 10% of revenue and be liable for user losses.
exec: A draft Korean law would allow a surcharge of a maximum of 10% of revenue for crypto businesses hacked after breaching IT safety duties, plus no-fault liability for user losses.
